name: approach to neonatal care overview
title: The newborn needing extra care, sorted by what it must be kept: pink (resuscitation at birth, then respiratory distress told apart by who, timing and chest x-ray), warm (hypothermia), sweet (hypoglycemia screening and treatment), free of sepsis (risk, workup, antibiotics) and the yellow baby (jaundice red flags, investigations, phototherapy); each column gives presentation, numbered assessment and treatment, with a panel on routine care before discharge

root.title: A newborn: keep it PINK, WARM and SWEET, and think SEPSIS in any sick baby
lines: normal: heart rate 120–160 · respiratory rate 40–60 · axillary temperature 36.5–36.8 °C · never ignore tachypnea or tachycardia

head: h
Resuscitation at birth
the goal: ventilation
clue: Term? good tone? breathing or crying?
• YES → skin to skin, routine care
• NO → warm, dry, position, stimulate, clear the airway
inv: → VENTILATE within the first minute + pulse oximeter
→ pulse oximeter, oxygen if needed, consider continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP)
tx: • oxygen saturation only 85–95% by 10 min: transient hypoxia is normal

head: h
Respiratory distress
work of breathing: grunting
clue: • term, cesarean with no labour: at birth, gets better
• preterm: at birth, worse to day 3–4
inv: • fluid in the fissures: transient tachypnea of the newborn
• ground glass, low volume, air bronchograms: respiratory distress syndrome (no surfactant)
tx: Pneumonia: any time, septic risk factors
group B Streptococcus, gram negatives → see SICK

head: h
Hypoglycemia
glycogen lasts 8–10 h · gluconeogenesis normal only by day 2–4
clue: can be a sign of SEPSIS
inv: 1 · Glucose 2 h after the first feed
≥ 3.3 after 72 h · at goal: no more sticks
tx: intravenous (IV) dextrose bolus + infusion: it injures neurons

head: h
Neonatal sepsis
the commonest life-threatening newborn problem · early < 3 days, late > 3 days
tx: 1 · Antibiotics ASAP: never wait and see

head: h
Jaundice
most: exaggerated physiologic or breastfeeding jaundice
clue: Head to toe: blanch the nose
colour does NOT predict the level
• jaundice in the first 24 h, or > 2 weeks (term)
inv: 1 · Bilirubin on EVERY baby at 24 h
skin meter or blood · plot on the curve
tx: start lower if < 38 weeks, albumin < 30, hemolysis, sepsis
2 · Not enough → IV immunoglobulin or exchange transfusion

panels.title: Every newborn before going home
items: Apgar at 1 and 5 min, 0–2 each: appearance, pulse (< 100 scores 1), grimace, activity (tone), respiration
full exam within 24 h: dysmorphic features, heart (may have no murmur), a patent gut · urine and meconium passed
vitamin K intramuscular + erythromycin eye ointment at birth
screens: pulse oximetry right hand vs a foot at 24–36 h · Ontario newborn screen · hearing
weight: loses up to 10%, back to birth weight by 7–10 days · seen 72 h after discharge
